title: The New High-entropy Compound RhMnFeCoGe4 with Cubic Non-centrosymmetric B20 Structure
authors: V. A. Sidorov, V. N. Krasnorussky, A. V. Bokov, Z. N. Volkova, A. P. Gerashchenko, N. M. Chtchelkatchev, M. V. Magnitskaya, D. A. Salamatin, A. V. Semeno, V. V. Brazhkin, A. V. Tsvyashchenko
abstract: A novel high-entropy compound, RhMnFeCoGe$_4$, with a cubic non-centrosymmetric B20 struc- ture, has been synthesized under conditions of high pressure and temperature. The electrical transport and magnetic properties of the obtained compound at both ambient and elevated pres- sures have been investigated. In addition, nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectra were obtained at 4.2 K and ab initio calculations were performed. The new material exhibits ferromag- netic behavior with a critical temperature of $T_C$ = 146 K and a spontaneous moment of 2.5 $μ_B$ per formula unit. The magnetization data obtained at the critical region yielded the critical temperature and exponents, which were found to be $T_C$ = 146(1) K, $β$ = 0.337(1), $γ$ = 1.121(1), and $δ$ = 4.326(1). The magnetic moments of Mn and Co were determined from NMR spectra to be 2.2 $μ_B$ and 0.5 $μ_B$, respectively. Ab initio calculations yielded reasonable values for the lattice parameter and the magnetic moments of all constituents. The density of states and band structure are determined for both paramagnetic and ferromagnetic states. Lattice compression results in the increase in the $T_C$.
summary: This work reports on the synthesis and comprehensive characterization of a novel high-entropy compound, RhMnFeCoGe4, which crystallizes in a B20 structure. The material is found to be ferromagnetic with a critical temperature of 146 K. By combining magnetic measurements, NMR spectroscopy, and DFT calculations, the authors map out its electronic structure and how its magnetic properties respond to external pressure.
main_problem: The study focuses on synthesizing and characterizing a novel high-entropy compound, RhMnFeCoGe4, which possesses a cubic non-centrosymmetric B20 structure.
main_result: The material exhibits ferromagnetic behavior with a critical temperature of 146 K and a spontaneous moment of 2.5 mu_B per formula unit, showing magnetic properties sensitive to external pressure.
method: A combination of experimental techniques (XRD, VSM, NMR) and theoretical calculations (ab initio DFT) was employed to investigate its electronic and magnetic structure.
model_or_system: The physical system is the high-entropy compound RhMnFeCoGe4, which adopts a cubic non-centrosymmetric B20 crystal structure. The research explores how magnetism and transport properties are governed by this complex composition under varying pressure conditions.
key_observables: Ferromagnetic ordering ($T_C=146$ K), spontaneous magnetization ($2.5 \mu_B$), critical exponents ($ eta, \gamma, \delta$), magnetic moments of constituent atoms (Mn: $2.2 \mu_B$, Co: $0.5 \mu_B$), and lattice parameters.
important_parameters: Critical temperature ($T_C=146$ K), applied pressures (up to 8 GPa), temperatures (2–260 K), and magnetic fields ($\le 9$ T).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the observed resistivity anomaly is due to chemical disorder, which was not fully accounted for in the initial *ab initio* simulations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate XRD patterns confirming the B20 structure; magnetization vs. temperature/field curves show ferromagnetic transitions and critical behavior; DOS and band structures compare paramagnetic and ferromagnetic states.
paper_structure: The paper follows a standard materials science investigation: synthesis confirmation (XRD) $ightarrow$ bulk magnetic characterization (VSM, critical exponents) $ightarrow$ microscopic analysis (NMR, DFT calculations of DOS/band structure) $ightarrow$ discussion of pressure effects.
why_interesting: While primarily condensed matter physics, the detailed study of magnetic phase transitions and electronic band structures in complex, disordered materials like high-entropy alloys touches upon many-body interactions relevant to correlated electron systems.

figures.caption: Figure 1: The XRD pattern of the RhMnFeCoGe4 compound. The blue dots represent the experimental data, the red line - fitting by Rietveld method, the gray line depicts the difference between the experiment and fitting, and the green ticks indicate the Bragg positions for the B20 structure. Asterisks denote the most intense peaks from the Fe1.67Ge impurity.

Figure 2: The temperature dependence of the magnetic susceptibility M/(µ0H) of the RhMnFeCoGe4 compound (left scale), measured in a field of µ0H = 0.01 T, and inverse magnetic susceptibility χ−1 = (µ0H)/M as a function of temperature (right scale). Red line - is a Curie-Weiss fit of χ−1 in a linear high-T region with µef f = 4.0 µB/f.u. and Curie-Weiss temperature Θ = 186 K.

Figure 3: Isotherms of magnetization of the RhMnFeCoGe4 compound for temperatures in the range 2-260 K (panel a), spontaneous magnetization MS , obtained at µ0H = 9 T as a function of temperature (panel b).

Figure 4: The magnetization of the RhMnFeCoGe4 compound, obtained at T = 2.0 K. Inset - an expanded region in proximity of µ0H = 0. The numbered arrows illustrate the variation in µ0H, which is represented by the following sequence: 1) an initial increase up to 9 T (black line), 2) a decrease in the field (red), and 3) a subsequent increase (blue).

Figure 5: The magnetic phase diagram of the RhMnFeCoGe4 compound. The points were identified as local minimums of the second derivative of the magnetization curve, the line is a guide for the eye. Inset demonstrate M(µ0H) (points) and d2M/d(µ0H)2 (line) dependencies as a function of magnetic field µ0H at T = 5 K. The position of the µ0HC2 is indicated by a vertical dashed line.
